Read materialized SCTA ST I q19 a3–5,7–8,10 and pinned Elwes Spinoza Ethics I definitions/axioms,16–17,29–33. Aquinas explicitly proposes self-determination of necessary will toward nonnecessary secondary objects (a3 ad5–6), distinguishes a cause of the single act from rational ordering of its objects (a5), and rejects secondary-cause defect as sufficient contingency explanation (a8). Spinoza I33 note II grants will as essence for an internal objection: different complete decrees imply different actual intellect/will and hence essence. His freedom means action from own nature (definition 7), not contingent choice. Rejected self-sufficiency-alone as proof of contingent willing, no-cause as no-object-reasons, temporal immutability as cross-world identity, and varying world-label tables as explanatory free creation. Detailed exact locators, strongest replies, rejected readings and remaining gaps persist in docs/notes/selected-effect-bridge-462.md, source follow-up. No new result, premise establishment or root-premise change.
